newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premium slips, market lacks fresh leads.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premium slips, market lacks fresh leads.

text.p: Thai sugar premiums slipped again this week in the absence of fresh positive leads, industry sources said on Monday.
January/March delivery was bid at 0.80-0.85 cents a pound over New York futures from about 0.92-0.95 last week.
March/May delivery was bid at 0.75-0.80 cents over New York March from 0.78-0.80 a week earlier.
"There's no fresh positive news to support the market," one trader said. "The demand is slow while there are reports of better-than-expected crops everywhere."
India, for example, had indicated that its production for the 1996/97 season might top 17 million tonnes, much higher than estimated by international analysts.
Traders said they did not expect the Thai sugar premium to move significantly next week.
On the production side, Thai sugar authorities would meet this week to discuss cane prices as the crushing season was to start soon, a Cane and Sugar Board official said.

The Sugar Board's preliminary figure for sugar cane production for 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) was 60.32 million tonnes and 6.28 tonnes tel quel for sugar output, compared with 57.69 million and 6.03 million respectively for 1995/96.
The Sugar Board is a separate body from the Cane and Sugar Board.
The Sugar Board would officially release the figures, which are used as a base for cane price calculations, early next month, the official told Reuters.
Its figures tend to differ from those of the agriculture ministry.
The ministry's sugar cane forecast was based on cane output while the sugar board's figure was usually based on the amount of cane expected to be crushed.
The agriculture ministry earlier this month revised the 1996/97 sugar cane forecast to 61.53 million tonnes from 62.42 million due to floods.
At Thai ports, there were no new declarations and sugar freight movement was slow this week.
About 37,000 tonnes of sugar had been shipped between October 11-21, all to Asian markets.
Vessel Orient Express is scheduled to arrive on October 31 to load 1,000 tonnes of white sugar to be shipped to Cambodia. Tate & Lyle was the buyer.
